FOREWORD `Illis Indian Standard (Part 63) (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft final ized by the Environment Protection and Waste Management Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. `Oxygen absorbed in 4 h' is useful for quick assessment of pollution potential of wastewater. This requirement is useful particularly when it is not feasible to conduct Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD) test due to interference by toxic substances. `['he Committee responsible for the formulation of IS 3025: 1964 `Methods of sampling and test (physical and them ica!) for water used in industry' had decided to revise the standard and publish it as separate parts. This standard is one of the different parts under the 1S 3025 series of standards and supersede 51 of IS 3025. There is no ISO Standard on the subject. This standard has been formulated based on the indigenous
prevalent in the field in India.

IS 3025 (Part 63) :2007

Indian Standard METHODS OF SAMPLING AND TEST (PHYSICAL AND CHEMICAL) FOR WATER AND WASTEWATER
PART 63 OXYGEN ABSORBED IN 4 h

(First Revision)
1 SCOPE This standard (Part 63) prescribes method of test for determination of oxygen absorbed in 4 h in water and wastewater. 2 REFERENCES The standards listed below contain provisions which through reference in this text constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. AII standards are subject to revision and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of the standards indicated below: IS No. 3025 (Part 1) : 1987 17t[e Methods of sampling (physical and chemical) and wastewater : Part 1 (first revision) and test for water Sampling level of wastewater, particularly when it is not feasible to conduct BOD test due to interference of toxic substances. It is usefid for laboratories with limited facilities. 6 RANGE AND APPLICABILITY

The range of the method depends upon the nature of sample as well as the requirement of potassium permanganate standard solution. The minimum detection limit of this method is 0.4 mg/1. 7 INTERFERENCE Excessive amount of residual chlorine interfe~e with the test. Inorganic substances such as nitrite, sulphide and ferrous iron react with potassium permanganate and get oxidized. 8 APPARATUS 8.1 Incubator or Water-Bath -- Suitable to maintain at 37 * 1�C. 8.2 Air Oven -- Suitable for use at 105 + 1�C. 9 REAGENTS 9.1 Stock Potassium Permanganate Solution -- Dissolve 3.951 g of potassium permanganate (dried at 105�C) in distilled water and make up to 1000 ml. This solution shall be kept in the dark and its strength shall be checked periodically, 9.2 Standard Potassium Permanganate Solution -- N/80 -- This solution shall be prepared immediately before use by suitable dilution of stock potassium permanganate solution. One millilitre of this solution is equivalent to 0.1 mg of oxygen. 9.3 Dilute Sulphuric Acid -- Add slowly 50 ml of concentrated sulphuric acid to 130 ml of distilled water, cool and make up to 200 ml with distilled water. Add standard permanganate solution until a very faint pink colour persists atler 4 h. 9.4 Potassium Iodide Crystals 9.5 Stock Sodium Thiosulphate 1 Solution -- Dissolve

7022 (Part 1) : 1973

Glossary of terms relating to water, sewage and industrial effluents : Part 1 Glossary of terms relating to water, sewage and industrial effluents : Part 2

7022 (Part 2) : 1979

3 TERMINOLOGY For the purpose of this standard, definitions given in 1S 7022 (Part 1) and IS 7022 (Part 2) shall apply. 4 SAMPLING AND PRESERVATION shall be done as

Sampling and sample preservation prescribed in IS 3025 (Part 1). 5 PRINCIPLE

Oxygen absorbed in 4 h is determined by estimating amount of standard potassium permanganate solution consumed by the sample kept under specific conditions in 4 h. This test is useful for quick assessment of pollution

IS 3025 (Part 63):2007 31.2 g of sodium thiosulphate and 6 g of sodium bicarbonate in water and make up to 1000 ml. 9.6 Standard Sodium Thiosttlphate Solution -- N/80 -- This shall be prepared by suitable dilution of stock sodium thiosulphate solution. Before using the solution the strength shall be checked by titration with standard potassium permanganate solution. 9.7 Starch Indicator Solution cool to about 15�C, add a few crystals of potassium iodide and titrate in the bottle with standard sodium thiosulphate solution, using a few drop of starch indictor solution. A blank for oxygen absorbed in 3 min shall be carried out. Express the result to the nearest 0.05 mg/1.
NOTE -- The measured volume of standard potassium permanganate solution taken shall be not less than 10 ml, but shall be such that at the end of 4 h, the amount remaining unchanged is between 5 and 15 ml. If it is found that the vohrme required was anticipated incorrectly, the determination shall be repeated.

10 PROCEDURE
Place 250 ml of the well-mixed sample into a clean, glass-stoppered bottle of 400 ml capacity. Add 10 ml dilute su~phuric acid, followed by an accurately measured volume (see Note) of standard potassium permanganate solution. Mix the contents by gentle rotations and place in a water-bath or incubator at 37+ 1`C for 4 h. If the sample contains much suspended matter, it shall be mixed by gentle rotation several times during the period of incubation. At the end of 4 h,

11 CALCULATION Oxygen absorbed in 4 h, mg/1 = 0.4 V where V= volume of standard potassium permanganate solution consumed in reaction with the sample, in ml.
